core_obligations: Factor the morphism (proof lines 6793-6801): the author factors f as the composite of a morphism h which is integral, universally injective and surjective and a closed immersion i, displayed as a diagram.

Apply the two companion results (proof lines 6802-6806): the closed immersion case is applied to i and topological invariance is applied to h, and the two results combine into both parts of the statement together with the assertion that the inverse image is a left inverse.
proof_roadmap: Factor the given morphism into an integral, universally injective and surjective morphism followed by a closed immersion.
Apply the closed immersion result to the second factor.
Apply topological invariance to the first factor and combine the two descriptions of the essential image.
difficulty_reason: The proposition treats the pushforward along a morphism that is integral and universally injective: on sheaves of sets it is fully faithful with essential image described by the complement of the image, and on abelian sheaves it is fully faithful with essential image the sheaves supported in the image, the inverse image being a left inverse in both cases (statement lines 6764-6791). The proof is a complete reduction: the author factors f into an integral, universally injective surjective morphism followed by a closed immersion (proof lines 6793-6801) and then applies the established closed immersion proposition to the second factor and topological invariance to the first (proof lines 6802-6806). The non-formal content is the factorization and the observation that the two known results are exactly the two factors. The claim is H2: a reduction whose two inputs are named.
